question: Does year-to-year precipitation immediately before breeding interact with island snow-retention habitat to explain deviations from the otherwise shared regional Adelie population trajectory?

response.annual_growth: log1p(N_i,t) - log1p(N_i,t-1) for adjacent annual censuses
response.extinction_rule: retain the positive-to-zero extinction transition; exclude zero-to-zero post-extinction intervals
response.local_deviation: island annual growth minus the mean annual growth of all other eligible islands in the same interval

weather_source.title: Daily averaged weather timeseries at Palmer Station, Antarctica

predictor.annual_metric: number of October calendar days immediately before the November census with numeric daily precipitation > 0
predictor.missingness: a year is eligible only when at least 25 October days have numeric precipitation observations
predictor.standardization: z-score eligible-year October precipitation-day counts across the frozen census interval

static_island_modifier.name: fraction of breeding habitat classified as suboptimal/snow-prone
static_island_modifier.role: external physical-habitat vulnerability modifier; values are topographic/hillshade-derived but were previously associated with population decline, so this interaction test is a synthesis/follow-up rather than a wholly independent habitat discovery

primary_model.leave_one_year_out: refit both models after withholding all island observations from one interval end-year

falsification: full model does not improve leave-one-year-out RMSE
effect depends on Litchfield post-extinction zero-to-zero intervals, which are excluded by design
October precipitation coverage fails the predeclared 25-day completeness rule for too many years to retain at least 15 annual intervals
secondary_descriptive_outputs: island-specific correlation between local deviation and October precipitation days
interaction residuals by island and year
prohibited_claims: precipitation is equivalent to measured island snow depth
the habitat modifier is independent fresh evidence because its published definition has already been related to population decline
absence of the interaction means island physical filtering is unimportant
next_gate: Only after this result is frozen, open a separate regional sea-ice mechanism lane with its own predeclared temporal alignment.
